text:
maya: Heads up — during a dry-run deprovision on staging the SCIM provisioner removed user memberships but a service-account principal still had KMS grants. Looks like grants weren't revoked when group->principal mapping was cleared. :confused:
sam: ugh — do you have the raw logs or steps?
maya: pasted the relevant lines from the provisioner run:
```
2026-03-19T22:12:34Z provisioner: delete membership user:alice from group:db-admins -> success
2026-03-19T22:12:34Z kms-sync: lookup principal for group:db-admins -> found arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-service-db
2026-03-19T22:12:34Z provisioner: mark group tombstone -> ok
2026-03-19T22:12:35Z kms-sync: revoke grant -> ERROR grant not found (grant id X)
2026-03-19T22:12:35Z kms-sync: fallback: leave existing policy in place
```
liam: that ERROR suggests the sync tried to revoke a grant that had already rotated/been removed earlier but the key policy still references the principal. We need to distinguish grants vs key policy principals.
irene: can you run a quick check in staging to confirm the principal still has decrypt/GenerateDataKey perms?
maya: ran this: `aws kms get-key-policy --key-id alias/redwood-prod-alias` -> policy still has "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-service-db"}
provisioner-bot: automated note: last successful full-kms-reconcile finished 2026-03-19T21:00:02Z
sam: timeline hypothesis: SCIM deprovision removed group membership and tombstoned group object, but the KMS sync reads group->principal mapping from an external cache that lagged. If tombstone path uses external_id rename, the lookup returned stale mapping and attempted grant revocation using an old grant id. The key policy remained because revocation path only touches grants, not policies.
liam: agreed. Short-term mitigation: run a targeted reconcile that removes principals from key policies that are no longer present in SCIM group mappings. I can run a script to diff principal lists and produce a safe update plan.
irene: +1. Also add a guard in the provisioner: when group is tombstoned, enqueue full-kms-sync for that tenant and mark the tombstone until reconcile completes. Prevents immediate reuse/race.
maya: will open an incident and assign action items. For the record: no production data was exposed — this was staging. Still worth a fix because same path exists for Dedicated customers.
sam: action items: 1) run liam's reconcile on staging and confirm key policies cleaned (sam, ongoing). 2) add tombstone -> enqueue sync behavior (maya + infra). 3) add audit event for key-policy changes and surface in console (irene + product). 4) add unit/integration test for grant vs policy drift (eng-ml/serving?).
liam: PR for reconcile script coming in a bit. Plan to produce a dry-run diff first: `python tools/kms_reconcile.py --tenant redwood-staging --dry-run`
irene: also please add a telemetry event so we can alert when policy-principal count != scim group members for any key > threshold.
maya: noted. I'll create the incident doc and add postmortem template. tagging @oncall for awareness. :eyes: 
sam: thanks — prioritize for patch release to provisioner before we hit Dedicated rollouts.
liam: update: dry-run shows 3 principals in key policy for alias/redwood-prod-alias that aren't in SCIM mappings. Will send diff and apply with approval.
maya: closing loop: after reconcile applied, follow-up task to run an audit job nightly for 7 days. We'll capture results in the incident doc.
provisioner-bot: deploy pipeline: provisioner-service v2.14.1 queued with tombstone-fix branch
maya: perfect. moving this to incident tracker and adding a short-term customer-impact check-list. thanks everyone.
